words.gloss: the destitute / those who have not
those who do not perform penance

literal: The reason why those who have not are many is that those who perform penance are few, and those who do not perform penance are many.
translation: The reason why the destitute are so numerous in this world is that those who practice self-discipline are very few, while those who do not are many.
modern: உலகில் வறியவர்கள் பலராக இருப்பதற்குக் காரணம், தவம் (சுயகட்டுப்பாடு) மேற்கொள்பவர்கள் சிலராகவும், அதனை மேற்கொள்ளாதவர்கள் பலராகவும் இருப்பதே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the disparity in human achievement and well-being through the lens of self-discipline or penance (tavam). The poet states that the reason why there are so many 'have-nots' (ilar) in the world is directly linked to a lack of effort and self-restraint. Those who undergo the rigorous practice of penance (nōṟpār) are very few, whereas those who avoid such discipline (nōlātavar) make up the vast majority. By equating the lack of penance with being a 'have-not', the couplet emphasizes that true wealth, power, and success are the fruits of sustained self-discipline and endurance.
